title: Exact kriging cross-validation from a covariance matrix — kcv_engine
text: ordinary/universal kriging (beta = NULL, trend re-estimated GLS fold): \(Q = C^{-1} - C^{-1}F(F'C^{-1}F)^{-1}F'C^{-1}\); simple kriging (known beta): \(Q = C^{-1}\), applied \(y - F\beta\). fold \(\), residual \(e_I = Q_{II}^{-1}(Qy)_I\), prediction \(y_I - e_I\), prediction-error variance \(\mathrm{diag}(Q_{II}^{-1})\). diagonal blocks \(Q_{II}\) formed, never full \(n \times n\) matrix \(Q\). Leave-one-(every fold size one) uses \(e_i = (Qy)_i / Q_{ii}\) \(1 / Q_{ii}\) directly.

title: Exact kriging cross-validation from a covariance matrix — kcv_engine
code: set.seed(1) xy <- matrix(runif(100), ncol = 2) C <- exp(-as.matrix(dist(xy)) / 0.3) y <- rnorm(50) res <- kcv_engine(C, matrix(1, 50, 1), y, folds = seq_len(50)) head(res$pred) #>             [,1] #> [1,] -1.25265287 #> [2,]  0.29321589 #> [3,]  0.43726382 #> [4,]  0.01225811 #> [5,] -0.04605711 #> [6,] -0.27491546  # Factorize once, then cross-validate several fold schemes. p <- kcv_engine_prepare(C, matrix(1, 50, 1)) loo <- kcv_engine_run(p, y, seq_len(50)) k5 <- kcv_engine_run(p, y, rep(1:5, 10))

title: Summary statistics of a cross-validation — kcv_metrics
text: residuals \(e_i\) (observed minus predicted), kriging variances \(\sigma_i^2\) z-scores \(z_i = e_i / \sigma_i\): rmse: \(\sqrt{\mathrm{mean}(e_i^2)}\); mae: \(\mathrm{mean}(|e_i|)\); bias: \(\mathrm{mean}(e_i)\) (positive predictions low average); mean_z, var_z: mean variance z-scores, ideally close 0 1. var_z uses \(n - 1\) denominator stats::var(), NA fold single observation; coverage_<100 L> level \(L\): proportion observations inside Gaussian prediction interval \(\hat y_i \pm q \sigma_i\), \(q\) = qnorm((1 + L) / 2), .e. \(|z_i| \le q\). Well-calibrated variances give coverage close \(L\). default levels 50, 80, 90 95% probe center tails predictive distribution. z-scores recomputed residual var1.var columns.

title: Factorize once, cross-validate many times — kcv_prepare
code: data(meuse, package = "sp") v <- gstat::vgm(0.59, "Sph", 897, 0.05) p <- kcv_prepare(log(zinc) ~ sqrt(dist), ~ x + y, meuse, model = v) p #> <kcv_prepared> universal kriging, n = 155, p = 2, 187.7 Kb loo <- kcv_run(p) set.seed(1) rmse_10fold <- replicate(5, sqrt(mean(kcv_run(p, nfold = 10)$residual^2))) rmse_10fold #> [1] 0.3876193 0.3918699 0.3886007 0.3739821 0.3781501 # Buffered leave-one-out at several radii from the same factorization. sapply(c(0, 200, 400), function(r) kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, buffer = r))$rmse) #> [1] 0.3771621 0.4349331 0.4640929  # New responses at the same locations: here 20 random permutations of # the observations, cross-validated from the same factorization. set.seed(2) perm <- replicate(20, sample(log(meuse$zinc))) cv_perm <- kcv_run(p, nfold = 10, y = perm) summary(kcv_metrics(cv_perm)$rmse) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.7316  0.8015  0.8146  0.8090  0.8259  0.8700

title: fastkcv 0.1.0
text: First release. kcv(): exact leave-one-k-fold cross-validation global simple, ordinary universal kriging one factorization covariance matrix. inputs (formula, locations, data, model, nfold, beta) output gstat::krige.cv(), data.frame, sf sp data; variogram models Nug, Exp, Sph, Gau, Mat, Ste, Cir, Pen, Bes, Wav, Hol, nested sums 2D geometric anisotropy. kcv_prepare() kcv_run(): factorize , cross-validate number fold schemes. Buffered leave-one-(buffer), optionally subset targets. Several responses one factorization: matrix left-hand side (cbind(z1, z2) ~ 1, matrix column) kcv() kcv_prepare(), new responses prepared object kcv_run(prepared, y = ), every fold scheme buffered leave-one-. output stacks one block per response response column; kcv_metrics() summarizes response. Simple kriging takes one beta responses p x T matrix (also kcv_run(beta = ) kcv_engine_run(beta = )). kcv_engine(), kcv_engine_prepare() kcv_engine_run(): computation precomputed covariance matrix, also matrix-valued response. Fold builders fold_random() (draw krige.cv(nfold = k)), fold_blocks() fold_kmeans(). kcv_metrics(): RMSE, MAE, bias, z-score mean variance, prediction-interval coverage, overall per fold. Memory requirements checked front getOption("fastkcv.max_gb"). Ordinary universal kriging estimate trend orthonormal basis trend matrix, trends large raw coordinates (quadratic trend UTM meters) stay accurate.
